content.thinking: I still need a sentence covering the still-at-risk item, so let me resubmit the whole thing.

action_items.item: Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after it was switched off at the flag provider.
Make io-shop pick up a flag switched off at the provider within a known, short time, and check this by switching off a test flag in production.
Alert when a flag's value at the provider and the value the service logs in its own evaluations disagree.
Have the Mitigation Agent check that the service's own flag evaluations show the new value before it judges a flag revert as having helped or not.
Until the fix is merged, turn monthly-spend-feature off in a way confirmed to reach io-shop's replicas.
Roll out flag changes on io-shop to a small share of traffic first, and watch the account page error rate before widening.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests answered with server errors rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average, peaking at {errors_at_worst}. The service's own account page error-rate warnings were at their highest at {Gbac1.7}.

From {began}, account page requests failed with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Before that minute, the only account page failures logged were shoppers closing the connection, and pages were logged as rendering normally.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. Deploys were read and none came back. The only production change found in the windows read was this flag switch.

The revision the replicas were running. All replicas ran one revision, and the service was measured healthy with it in place before the flag was switched on: errors were at their baseline and account pages were logged as rendering normally.

causal_chain.step: The spend-summary code ran because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. Before then the service evaluated the flag as off for every request. In the minute of the switch it evaluated the flag as on for part of its requests, and in each later minute over {Gce95.4} it evaluated it as on for all of them. The ZeroDivisionError failures began in that same minute.

With the flag on, account page requests reach `average_spend_per_item_this_month`. It divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases marked as in the current month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, and the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}. The failure reaches the account page. With the flag off, this path is not taken.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page made those pages fail, likely because the summary divides a shopper's spending this month by the number of things they bought this month, and that sum breaks for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Switching the flag off at the provider did not reach the service. The provider recorded monthly-spend-feature as off from {P2.1}, but the service still logged every evaluation of the flag as on in each minute over {Gce95.4}, and its account page error rate was at its highest at {Gbac1.7}.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Switching the flag off would have taken the failing path out of account page requests from {P2.1}, and the failures would likely have stopped there instead of continuing past the end of the record.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: In the files Code-Fix read, no test ran the monthly summary path with a shopper who had bought nothing this month. That kind of shopper already existed as a test fixture, and Code-Fix reads both of its proposed cases as raising ZeroDivisionError against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would likely have failed before the flag was ever switched on, and the division would have been found before it reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The flag reached all of the service's traffic at once. From the minute after it was switched on, every evaluation the service logged was on. No staged rollout to a small share of traffic was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A small share of account page requests would have failed while the error rate was watched, rather than every request the flag reached.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: No person was paged. No on-call incident was linked to the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have known about the failures when the alert fired. They could have stepped in once the flag revert did not help, rather than the incident going on until it was escalated with a draft fix.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well: The Investigator tied the failures to the flag switch, matching the ZeroDivisionError lines to the minute the flag went on. Argus reverted the flag {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The revert was made so it could be undone, and it was undone when it did not help.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request for a person to review {T39.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised. It holds a proposed fix and two tests that run the path the flag enables.
went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent took its first look {T21.1 - T19.1} after the revert. It then judged the revert refuted, and nothing in the record shows it checked whether the service now evaluated the flag as off. The service's logs show it still evaluating the flag as on, so the refutation was of a revert that had not taken effect.
Because the revert was judged refuted, the flag was put back on at {T22.1}.
The second investigation came back with the same flag as the cause. That candidate counted as already refuted, so Argus escalated without a working mitigation in place.

input.root_cause: Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests into `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases marked as in the current month and does not check whether that number is zero. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month the count is zero, so line {F1.1} raises ZeroDivisionError, and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: With monthly-spend-feature switched back on and the division still unguarded, account page requests from shoppers with nothing bought this month could keep failing, and switching the flag off at the provider had not been seen to reach the service.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
